id: Serenna With Tragedies And Diplopoda-MOON, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Serenna With Tragedies And Diplopoda
long_description:
Join us for a night of cathartic revelry at the end of the world with your local musical specters Serenna with support from Tragedies and Diplopoda. Prepare to be haunted, bewitched and entranced by melodic tunes of horror, beauty, heartache and triumph.

Established in 2003, Serenna formed out of an idea to challenge the listener with unsettling themes, wrapped in a beguiling veneer. After six years of serenading audiences in Wellington and further afield, the band fell silent. Now, as if keelhauled through the shit of existence, Serenna has arisen for the end times with a defiant brand of apocalyptic. Forged from neofolk and gothic rock influences, Serenna brings new and old tales of love, death and despair for those brave enough to listen.

Tragedies is a Pōneke based trio that blends elements of trip-hop, alt-rock and post-punk and explores the overlap of beauty and horror with ethereal harmonies, haunting melodies and moments of heavy industrial grit that invite the listener to be vulnerable and revel in the tragedies and triumphs of life.

Diplopoda rips into those emotions you suppress, to be seen is to feel. A solo post modern pop-punk artist based in Pōneke. With theatrical movements and scorned expressions her act is as much of a visual experience as a sonic one.

***FREE TICKETS FOR TRANS AND GENDERQUEER FOLKS, DM @TRAGEDIESNZ ON INSTA***

id: Uncle Chipper-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Uncle Chipper
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Uncle Chipper!

Uncle Chipper is comprised of 5 people. They are a modern Jazz quintet. Uncle Chipper’s mission statement is as follows: to honor the likeliness and embodiment of Uncle Chipper through beautiful music and palpable chippage. No one person of Uncle Chipper is Uncle Chipper, for they are merely nephews of Uncle Chipper, which collectively embody the group, Uncle Chipper. They, as nephews, will present the audience with a mix of elegant swing, free jazz, grime, gunk, and most importantly, happiness. These articles will be presented as follows, with Sascha Hunt on guitar, Sylvester Green on trumpet, Max Stopyra on bass, Logan Heppell tickling the ivories, Ranu Wijesuriya on drums, and a few mystery guests. You will not want to miss this.

Doors 7pm
Music 7:30pm
$15 ($10 students)

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

id: Awkwatch X Doggabarka-Valhalla, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Awkwatch X Doggabarka
long_description:
Electronic voice from the underground sound of the city re-emerges and presents producers, storytellers, and sit-alone-listeners eyes to three upcoming pillars of the Wellington music scene.

Electronic shoegaze duo Laluna open the show with blissful dreampop soundscapes and serene harmonic melodies, layered to breathe divine into space and time. Backed by a live band, Laluna grow their ethereal voice onstage, further expanding the encapsulating reverie of their musical catalogue.

Doggabarka, experimental electro rap artist, presents work from his latest release to his very first album. Chilling visuals and gritty noise art propels the unexpected maze of sound fronted by Doggabarka's lyrical storytelling. An air of mystery moves aggressive beats and industrial detail into hypnotic and addictive alt hip-hop creation.

Infecting audiences with his high energy stage presence and vibrant, ever-moving beats, Awkwatch bends influence of rap, hip-hop, and trap sound into a captivating presentation of electronic rhythm. Unusual synth play, boosted by travelling 808 bass, paints a sonic palette of vivid colour and honest creativity, harnessed by dynamic vocal staging.

Catch all three artists at Valhalla on Thursday, October 1st.

long_description:

id: Moon Goose Live-The BakeHouse Collective, Featherston, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Moon Goose Live
long_description:
Moon Goose are making their way to the Wairarapa for an evening of song, story, and music to move you deep and good. These strangely adorable creatures will warm your heart with their intricate harmonies, deep folk-scapes and glittering original songs.

Holly Dove (guitar, vocals, celtic whistle) Britta Hamill (fiddle, vocals) and Charlie Radford (double bass, vocals), play a mix of traditional songs from the British Isles alongside original music inspired by deep love for nature, friendship and the merging of our Celtic folk heritage with our lives as Pākeha in Aotearoa.

Following their debut EP On the Island Where Our Shadows Lie, Moon Goose has performed around the motu, including at Auckland Folk Festival, Raglan Folk Festival, and alongside Greta O'Leary, Fables and National Sensation.

- Thursday 1 October 2026
- The Bakehouse Collective, Featherston
- Doors 6:30pm | Music from 7pm
- Tickets: $20 waged / $15 unwaged

id: Samba Independente-Rogue and Vagabond, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Samba Independente
long_description:
October at The Rogue and Vagabond kicks off vibrant, with Samba Independente back on stage — this time joined by a special guest, superb flautist Annalisa Powell, all the way from Australia, adding a fresh new voice and promising some unforgettable musical interplay.
Expect the full spectrum of samba — from roots samba and samba rock to samba-canção, samba paulista, and samba de breque — delivered with the infectious energy Samba Independente is known for. Come catch the band's signature blend of rhythm and groove, this time with a special guest twist.

This time we are: Alda Rezende (vocals), Adriana Gimenes (percussion), Felicien Houet (guitar), Julie Bevan (cavaquinho), Matheus Peres (percussion, vocals), Nikkie Rich (percussion, vocals), Tomas Souza (percussion), and our special guest Annalisa Powell on flute.

Come move to the unmistakable pulse of samba.

Music from 8pm, FREE ENTRY

id: Neither Do I - Wellington-Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Neither Do I - Wellington
long_description:
Indie rock 4 piece Neither Do I will be playing their first run of shows outside of Auckland this October, starting with an intimate gig at Vogelmorn Upstairs, with support by local midwest emo duo Park Flyers and indie folk band Welcomer who just released a lovely album called Calendars, definitely check it out!
Based on the songwriting of Danny Ebdale, the 4 piece released their debut We're Not Known for Anything in April last year to a warm reception:

Ebdale has built an interesting body of work, largely out of earshot of a wider audience. But – as someone with a few touchstones in the Flying Nun ethos and some of Britain's observant Northern singer-songwriters – he's also conspicuously on his own course. Danny Ebdale is someone worth hearing and this album with numerous musicians (cello, violin, clarinet and vocals) is an assured step towards the greater attention he deserves. - Graham Reid, NZ Listener

A four year mammoth in the making, Danny has taken no shortcuts in delivering a masterful and deeply personal piece of work that is subtle, yet full of depth. Nine tracks fill the space, and while they all follow similarities of more personal storytelling, each track very much holds its own arrangement and careful nuances. - Kerry MB, muzic.nz

Very excited to play these shows! We will debut some new material as well - hope to see you there.

id: Moon Goose And Butter Wouldn't Melt-Bedlam And Squalor, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Moon Goose And Butter Wouldn't Melt
long_description:
Join us from 7-9 for a cosy evening of music and cocktails at Bedlam & Squalor, just above Rogue and Vagabond (access on left side of building, Level 1/ 18 Garrett Street).

Starting out as humble music-making pals, Moon Goose are realising their folk powers. These strangely adorable creatures will warm your heart with their intricate harmonies, deep folk-scapes and glittering original songs. On the back of their debut EP On the Island Where Our Shadows Lie, Moon Goose have been performing to audiences across the motu, showcasing their unique blend of Celtic-inspired folk music, featuring both traditional songs from the British Isles and original compositions that celebrate nature, friendship, and the timeless spirit of folk music. Holly Dove (guitar, Celtic whistle, vocals), Britta Hamill (fiddle, vocals) and Charlie Radford (double bass, vocals) invite you to join them for an immersive musical journey rich with story and magic. Their music will move you deep and good.

Wellington-based band Butter Wouldn’t Melt bring their own unique blend of folk music incorporating aspects of country and traditional with a distinctly New Zealand flavour defined by poetic lyricism, powerful harmonies and masterful instrumentation. Gathered around one microphone, Andrea Reid (rhythm guitar), Nick Burfield (lead guitar), Cara Brasted (fiddle), Marz Connelly (double bass), and Mikey Muggeridge (mandolin) are known for their high energy and joyful performances. They are ready to melt your hearts and kick dust up off the floor in a performance that can’t be missed.

Doors 6:30 pm
Music 7-9pm
Tickets $20
Support the artists $30

id: Liv.e and Karriem Riggins (GENA) The Pleasure Is Yours Tour-Meow, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Liv.e and Karriem Riggins (GENA) The Pleasure Is Yours Tour
long_description:
There is a kinetic energy that binds drummer and producer Karriem Riggins and singer-songwriter, rapper, and producer Liv.e—the spark that happens when instinct meets flow and spirit finds rhythm.
﻿
Their collaborative debut as GENA (short for “God Energy, Naturally Amazing,” and loosely inspired by Gina from Martin), The Pleasure Is Yours (via Lex Records), feels like a playful, soulful conversation between two kindred improvisers: Liv.e’s smoky, unpolished vocals glide through Riggins’ warm, percussive universe. Rooted in jazz, soul, and hip-hop as living language, the Dallas-born Liv.e brings a raw, experimental approach to R&B, while Detroit native Riggins—known for his work with Common, Erykah Badu, The Roots, Madlib, and a close kinship with the late J Dilla—extends his lifelong dialogue between jazz improvisation and beat science. Together they create a world that’s analog and ethereal, percussive and poetic, bridging eras without ever settling in one; The Pleasure Is Yours is the sound of Liv.e and Riggins bringing each other’s music to life and finding a new language together—one rooted in rhythm, vulnerability, and exuberance.

﻿

Support:

Te Whanganui-a-Tara based Tokelauan singer-songwriter Romi Wrights blends soul, funk, boogie and modern jazz with warm, expressive vocals and deeply personal storytelling, drawing on the spirit of classic late-’60s soul and R&B.

+

DJ and broadcaster Awa (Wainuiomata | Te Ātiawa l Ngāti Kahungunu l Ngāti Maniapoto) brings his signature mix of house, broken beat and global grooves from the airwaves to the dancefloor.

id: Film Screening: Listen To The Land Speak-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Film Screening: Listen To The Land Speak
long_description:
Join us on Friday 2nd October for the fifth of our film viewings. This free community event is an opportunity to meditate as a group, meet new people, share food and watch a beautiful film together. Bring a light snack to share.

Listen to the Land Speak (2025) follows Manchán Magan, Irish author, through four seasons as he explores the ways stories and myths will help us reconnect to the nature around us. The documentary takes a personal turn as Magan realises he has a serious illness and starts to see the rivers, mountains and lands around him in a whole new light. October 2nd will mark the one year anniversary of his death, join us to celebrate his life and this beautiful film.

Friday Oct 2
Start 6pm
Free entry

We’d love to see you there!

id: Rowena Wise - Debut New Zealand Solo Tour-Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Rowena Wise - Debut New Zealand Solo Tour
long_description:
Presented by The Slack Agency, Beloved Records, Remote Control Records:

This spring, Rowena Wise makes her long-awaited New Zealand debut, bringing an intimate solo show across the motu for the first time. With just voice and guitar, Rowena’s songs hit with a rare kind of clarity - tender, point-blank, and unafraid of the quietest truths.

From Melbourne to Auckland, Wellington to Oakura and beyond, the tour celebrates a body of work that holds space rather than demands attention, tracing heartbreak, estrangement, and the knottier growing pains of adulthood with candid poetic lyricism.

Since debuting in 2018, Rowena has amassed over 10 million streams, earned airplay across triple j, Double J and Unearthed, and toured extensively across Australia, the UK, Europe, the USA and Canada, supporting artists including Folk Bitch Trio, Holy Holy, Ball Park Music, Bernard Fanning and Paul Dempsey. Her 2024 debut album, Senseless Acts of Beauty, was praised by CLASH Magazine as “carefully etched indie folk” and shortlisted for the Australian Music Prize.
Expect favourites, new material, and the kind of stillness you can feel in your chest.

Carefully etched indie folk — CLASH Magazine
Fragrant introspection — FLOOD
